title: Two kids, 16 bloodhounds removed from 'unsafe and unsanitary' Ishpeming home - NewsBreak
text:
By Alexandria Bournonville ,
10 hours ago
ISHPEMING TOWNSHIP, Mich. (WBUP/WJMN) — Two people were arrested on domestic violence, child abuse, and animal neglect charges following an investigation in Ishpeming Township, according to Michigan State Police (MSP).
Reports of a domestic violence incident came in on Tuesday, June 23, around 8:10 p.m. Troopers determined the suspect left the residence and returned to his home in the city of Ishpeming. With a search warrant, MSP personnel searched the home.
Inside, troopers describe finding two young children, 16 bloodhound dogs, and one cat living in what they deemed "unsafe and unsanitary conditions." They added that the home contained "extensive animal feces and urine."
MSP personnel allegedly observed additional evidence "indicating that both the children and animals were not being properly cared for."
As a result, an adult male was arrested on the following charges:
Aggravated domestic violence
Domestic violence
Second-degree child abuse
Animal abuse/neglect
An adult female also living in the home was arrested on charges of second degree-child abuse and animal abuse/neglect. Both individuals were lodged in the Marquette County Jail.
In coordination with Child Protective Services (CPS), the children were placed with a relative to ensure their immediate safety while further investigation is done.
MSP confirmed these are the same dogs UPAWS took in on Tuesday that caused the shelter to reach full capacity. FURTHER READING | Emergency intake of 16 large dogs puts UPAWS at capacity, forces suspension of some services
